title: Surprising Success, Repeated Failure: Entropy-Guided Credit Assignment for Exploration in LLM Reasoning
data_curation: No new data is built. All optimization-based methods train on DAPO-Math-17k-Processed, with rule-based answer verification via Math-Verify. Rollouts are capped at 10,240 tokens for base models (soft overlong penalty from 8,192) and 38,912 for reasoning models (penalty from 32,768). The motivating analysis uses 20 moderately difficult problems per model (6-14 of 32 correct) from AIME24/25/26, HMMT26 and AMC23, plus a word-frequency study of 2,376 Qwen3-4B-Base responses comparing the top and bottom 10% entropy tails.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. EAPO is a single-stage RLVR run (100 rollout iterations, constant LR with 10 warmup steps) applied directly to base models (Qwen3-4B/8B-Base, scaling study 1.7B-14B) or to already-post-trained reasoning models (Qwen3-4B, Olmo-3-7B-Think-DPO), without an added SFT stage. Training uses a DAPO-style recipe: asymmetric clipping (0.2, 0.28), token-mean loss aggregation, soft overlong penalty, no KL or entropy bonus, and token-level TIS with cap 2.0.
method: EAPO (Entropic Advantage Policy Optimization) redistributes the GRPO response advantage across tokens using the sign of the advantage together with policy entropy. Token entropy under the old policy is normalized with batch-wide 10th/90th percentiles, clipped to [0,1] and detached (h). Each token gets weight w = exp(kappa*sign(A)*h) divided by its within-response mean, and the token advantage is A*w. Successful responses therefore reinforce high-entropy tokens more ('surprising success'), failed responses penalize low-entropy tokens more ('repeated failure'), and penalties at uncertain positions are attenuated to keep alternatives open. The mean advantage per response is preserved and weights differ by at most e^kappa; default kappa=log 4. Theory: the weights solve a KL-regularized allocation against uniform credit; stronger negative updates sharpen the distribution over unchosen tokens; and in a binary model success carries more information at high entropy, failure at low entropy. Setup: LoRA r=32, alpha=64, LR 1e-5, AdamW, 16 prompts x G=8, TRL+vLLM on a single H200.
eval_metrics: Avg@32 and unbiased pass@32 on 297 math problems: AIME24/25/26, HMMT26, AMC23 and MATH500 level-5 (MATH500-H), with six-benchmark means. OOD: avg@16 on eight Reasoning Gym tasks (graph coloring, cube rotation, mini sudoku, family, knights and knaves, anagrams, zebra, palindrome). Also pass@k up to 256 on AIME26, normalized answer entropy and collision rate on low-accuracy problems, and epistemic-marker frequency. Headline mean avg@32: Qwen3-4B-Base 31.0 and 8B-Base 34.0, beating the best entropy baselines by 5.6 and 4.3 points. Reasoning backbones: Qwen3-4B 72.4, Olmo-3-7B-Think-DPO 74.3. Reasoning Gym macro: 34.89 and 43.02. Answer entropy 0.751 vs 0.657 for GRPO; collision rate 0.101 vs 0.166.
key_results: EAPO gets the best mean avg@32 and pass@32 on all four backbones, beating GRPO, EntropyAdv, HAPO, 80/20 forking tokens, and the privileged-information method RLRT. On Qwen3-4B-Base AIME24 it reaches 20.2 avg@32 vs 12.5 for GRPO and 15.3 for RLRT. The sign-entropy ablation shows the (+1, -1) coupling beats uniform credit by 6.52 avg@32 points, and a surprisal-based variant collapses to zero reward.
evolution_note: EAPO extends the entropy-centric RLVR line that followed DAPO/GRPO (80/20 high-entropy forking tokens, EntropyAdv advantage bonuses, HAPO), which treats uncertainty the same way in successful and failed responses. It reacts to that symmetry with sign-dependent credit, and to fine-grained credit methods that need PRMs, value models, extra rollouts or privileged teachers (VinePPO, RLRT). In their place it offers a drop-in token-advantage reweighting computed from rollout entropy alone that broadens pass@k coverage, which matters for the RLVR exploration-collapse problem.
